description: Look up SEVERAL Bible passages in ONE call: exact text for up to 30 references, each with its own book, chapter, verses and optionally its own translation (the same passage in two translations is two entries). Use this instead of several bible_lookup calls whenever more than one passage is needed. Results come back in request order; an entry that fails carries `fehler` and does not fail the others. Never quote from memory: an entry without `text` was not delivered. Editions that cap verbatim quoting apply the cap to the whole call (all entries of that edition together); entries beyond it come back with `ohne_wortlaut` and no text, and `hinweis` says so.

stellen.description: The passages, 1 to 30 entries, answered in this order.

translation.description: Translation code for this entry only; overrides the call-wide `translation`.

verses.description: Verse(s): single "4", range "16-17", list "1,3,5", or combined "1-3,7". Omit for the whole chapter.

translation.description: Translation for all entries that do not name their own: "LUT" (Luther 1912), "SCH" (Schlachter 1951), "ELB" (Elberfelder 1871), "MB" (Menge 1939), "SLT" (Schlachter 2000). Default: "SLT" (Schlachter 2000). Aliases like "luther", "schlachter" accepted. Only editions this instance actually loaded can be requested; bible_server_info lists them.

name: bible_lookup_many

verse_max.description: Maximum verses this edition may quote per call, across all entries.

ohne_wortlaut.description: Entries beyond a verbatim cap, without text.

stellen.description: One entry per requested passage, in request order. An entry carries either `text`, or `fehler`, or `ohne_wortlaut`.

anfrage.description: The passage as requested, on entries that carry no `reference`.

fehler.description: Why this entry could not be looked up. The other entries are unaffected.

gekuerzt.description: Present only when the edition's verbatim cap cut this entry short; `reference` names the verses it does contain.

kurzref.description: Short German citation form of what this entry contains. Copy into prose.

nr.description: Position in the request, starting at 1.

ohne_wortlaut.description: True when the passage exists but the edition's verbatim cap for this call was already used up. Its text is not in this response; do not supply it from memory.
